en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll learn have and have got, the English words for 'punya'. We'll talk about family, things and what people look like, one small step at a time.

steps.title: have and has
steps.text: In Indonesian you say *punya*. In English you say **have**, but it changes with he, she and it.
steps.body: Use **have** for your **family** and the **things you own**. With **I, you, we, they** say **have**: I have a sister. With **he, she, it** say **has**: My sister has a son. Never `she have` or `he haves`. Remember: one person or thing (Sari, my father, the shop) = he/she/it → **has**.

steps.title: Family and things
steps.text: Here are some real sentences. Look at have and has.
steps.body: *punya* never changes in Indonesian, so check the subject every time.

examples.en: My parents have a warung in Bandung.
examples.id: Orang tua saya punya warung di Bandung.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Let's try one. Who is the subject?

question.prompt: Complete: Pak Hasan ___ two sons and a daughter.
question.explanation: Pak Hasan = he, so use **has**. Don't put is before have: `is have` is wrong.

steps.title: have got = have
steps.text: You'll often hear **have got**, especially in British English. Good news: it means the same as have.
steps.body: For family, things and appearance, **have got** = **have**: I've got two brothers = I have two brothers. It is usually short: **I've got**, **she's got**. Before *got*, **'s = has**, not *is*: she's got = she has got. For actions use only have: I **have** breakfast at six (not `I've got breakfast`).

steps.title: Listen
steps.text: Press play and listen to the sentence. Think about the short 's.

question.prompt: Listen. What does He's mean in this sentence?
question.explanation: You heard: *He's got a new phone.* Before **got**, 's always means **has**: He has got a new phone.

steps.title: What people look like
steps.text: Now let's describe people: hair, eyes, a beard.
steps.body: Use **have/has (got)** + adjective + noun: She has long hair. He's got a beard. Indonesian says *Rambutnya panjang*, but don't say `She is long hair`. Say **She has long hair** or **Her hair is long**. Put length before colour: **long black hair**. And **hair** has no -s: long hair, not `long hairs`.

steps.title: Build a sentence
steps.text: Describe Dewi. Remember: length first, then colour.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Rambut Dewi panjang dan hitam.
question.explanation: Subject + **has** + adjectives + **hair**: Dewi has long black hair. Dewi = she → has, and length (long) comes before colour (black).

steps.title: Negatives and questions
steps.text: Here are two systems. Pick one and don't mix them.
steps.body: **have** works like other verbs: I **don't have**, she **doesn't have**, **Do** you have ...? — Yes, I do. **have got** uses have/has itself: I **haven't got**, she **hasn't got**, **Have** you got ...? — Yes, I have. Never `Do you have got ...?`, never `she doesn't has`, and don't say `I haven't a car`.

pairs.en: Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
Yes, she has. / No, she hasn't.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Budi goes to work by bus. Why? Pick the correct negative.

question.prompt: Complete: Budi ___ a motorbike. He goes to work by bus.
question.explanation: After **doesn't**, use the base form **have**, not has. `haven't` needs **got**, and Budi = he, so it would be hasn't got.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: It's raining and you need an umbrella. Ask your friend.

question.prompt: Complete: ___ you got an umbrella? It's raining.
question.explanation: With **got**, the question starts with **Have**: Have you got ...? Don't use Do with got, and don't use Are.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here is everything on one page. Keep it for later.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · have / have got

examples.en: I've got two brothers and a sister.
examples.id: Saya punya dua saudara laki-laki dan satu saudara perempuan.

examples.en: Do you have a motorbike? — No, I don't.

steps.text: Want more practice? This British Council page explains have got with exercises.

id.greeting: Halo! Hari ini kamu akan belajar have dan have got, kata bahasa Inggris untuk 'punya'. Kita akan membicarakan keluarga, barang dan ciri fisik orang, pelan-pelan satu langkah setiap kali.

steps.title: have dan has
steps.text: Dalam bahasa Indonesia kita bilang *punya*. Dalam bahasa Inggris pakai **have**, tapi bentuknya berubah untuk he, she dan it.
steps.body: Pakai **have** untuk **keluarga** dan **barang milikmu**. Dengan **I, you, we, they** pakai **have**: I have a sister. Dengan **he, she, it** pakai **has**: My sister has a son. Jangan bilang `she have` atau `he haves`. Ingat: satu orang atau benda (Sari, my father, the shop) = he/she/it → **has**.

steps.title: Keluarga dan barang
steps.text: Ini beberapa kalimat nyata. Perhatikan have dan has.
steps.body: *punya* tidak pernah berubah dalam bahasa Indonesia, jadi selalu cek subjeknya.

examples.en: My parents have a warung in Bandung.
examples.id: Orang tua saya punya warung di Bandung.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Yuk coba satu. Siapa subjeknya?

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Pak Hasan ___ two sons and a daughter.
question.explanation: Pak Hasan = he, jadi pakai **has**. Jangan taruh is sebelum have: `is have` salah.

steps.title: have got = have
steps.text: Kamu akan sering mendengar **have got**, terutama di bahasa Inggris Britania. Kabar baiknya: artinya sama dengan have.
steps.body: Untuk keluarga, barang dan ciri fisik, **have got** = **have**: I've got two brothers = I have two brothers. Biasanya disingkat: **I've got**, **she's got**. Sebelum *got*, **'s = has**, bukan *is*: she's got = she has got. Untuk kegiatan pakai have saja: I **have** breakfast at six (bukan `I've got breakfast`).

steps.title: Dengarkan
steps.text: Tekan play dan dengarkan kalimatnya. Perhatikan 's yang pendek.

question.prompt: Dengarkan. Apa arti He's dalam kalimat ini?
question.explanation: Kamu mendengar: *He's got a new phone.* Sebelum **got**, 's selalu berarti **has**: He has got a new phone.

steps.title: Ciri fisik seseorang
steps.text: Sekarang kita deskripsikan orang: rambut, mata, jenggot.
steps.body: Pakai **have/has (got)** + kata sifat + kata benda: She has long hair. He's got a beard. Bahasa Indonesia bilang *Rambutnya panjang*, tapi jangan bilang `She is long hair`. Katakan **She has long hair** atau **Her hair is long**. Panjang-pendek dulu, lalu warna: **long black hair**. Dan **hair** tanpa -s: long hair, bukan `long hairs`.

steps.title: Susun kalimat
steps.text: Deskripsikan Dewi. Ingat: panjang-pendek dulu, lalu warna.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Rambut Dewi panjang dan hitam.
question.explanation: Subjek + **has** + kata sifat + **hair**: Dewi has long black hair. Dewi = she → has, dan panjang (long) ada sebelum warna (black).

steps.title: Kalimat negatif dan pertanyaan
steps.text: Ada dua sistem. Pilih salah satu dan jangan dicampur.
steps.body: **have** seperti kata kerja lain: I **don't have**, she **doesn't have**, **Do** you have ...? — Yes, I do. **have got** memakai have/has itu sendiri: I **haven't got**, she **hasn't got**, **Have** you got ...? — Yes, I have. Jangan bilang `Do you have got ...?`, jangan `she doesn't has`, dan jangan `I haven't a car`.

pairs.en: Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
Yes, she has. / No, she hasn't.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Budi ke kantor naik bus. Kenapa? Pilih bentuk negatif yang benar.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Budi ___ a motorbike. He goes to work by bus.
question.explanation: Setelah **doesn't**, pakai bentuk dasar **have**, bukan has. `haven't` butuh **got**, dan Budi = he, jadi seharusnya hasn't got.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Hujan turun dan kamu butuh payung. Tanya temanmu.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: ___ you got an umbrella? It's raining.
question.explanation: Dengan **got**, pertanyaan diawali **Have**: Have you got ...? Jangan pakai Do dengan got, dan jangan pakai Are.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini semuanya dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk nanti, ya.
